exposure: daytime ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) cut-off points
nocturnal ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) cut-off points
cohort: The study included 1374 high-risk pregnant women, excluding those receiving antihypertensive treatment at the time of ABPM measurement.
finding: The study suggests that the current nocturnal ABPM threshold (120/70 mmHg) is appropriate for identifying PE risk after 30 weeks, but lower thresholds (around 115/65 mmHg) may be better for 20-27 weeks, and consistently lower daytime thresholds (e.g., 120-130/75-80 mmHg) are more suitable across both gestational periods than currently recommended.
